transcript.content: Hello, I am Dr. Smith. Could you please tell me what brings you in to see me today?

Hello, Dr. Smith. I'm here because I can’t stop thinking about how old and wrong my face looks, and it’s getting in the way of me moving up at work. It has just become really overwhelming lately and I'm not sure what to do.
Do you feel that others around you, like your coworkers, are also judging your appearance or talking about your face behind your back?

Yes, some of my younger coworkers made subtle comments about "looking professional on camera," which made me feel really self-conscious. It convinced me that they, and others, probably see my face as too worn out and old for a leadership role, even though I don't have direct proof they are gossiping behind my back.
Do you feel absolutely certain that your coworkers are judging your face, or is there a part of you that wonders if you might be misinterpreting their comments?

While I know their comments were technically just about looking professional on camera, I feel deeply convinced they were judging my aging face. Even though my husband reassures me and a small part of me wishes I could ignore it, I just can't shake the intense feeling that everyone will look at my wrinkles and sagging skin and decide I'm too worn out to be a leader.

Do you feel that your belief about your appearance is an objective fact that cannot be disproven, or are you able to acknowledge that your perception of your face might be exaggerated or distorted by your own worries?

To be honest, it feels incredibly real to me when I look in the mirror, and it's hard to see it any other way. I'm just not sure how to answer whether it's an objective fact or if my worries are distorting things. It just feels so completely true to me, even if others tell me otherwise.
Do you feel that your conviction is so absolute that you would consider it a fact, even if you were shown evidence or told by others that your face looks normal for your age?

I'm really not sure if I would call it an absolute fact, but it feels so incredibly real to me that it's hard to ignore. Even when people tell me I look normal for my age, I just can't bring myself to believe them because of what I see. It just feels too true to dismiss, even if I want to.
Do you spend significant time performing repetitive behaviors, such as checking your reflection in mirrors or seeking constant reassurance about your appearance, because of these thoughts?

Yes, most days I spend 20 to 30 minutes in front of the bathroom mirror before work pulling my skin back, trying different makeup, and taking and deleting selfies to check how bad I look. I also constantly ask my husband over and over if I look too old to be on video calls.
